scenes.headline: Threefold Faith
visual: You are what you believe in
scenes.say: Chapter Seventeen. Threefold Faith. What we believe in, Krishna says, shapes who we become.

scenes.headline: Faith without the rule book
visual: Who do not follow the scriptures?
scenes.say: Arjuna asks a sincere question. What about people who practise with faith, but without following the scriptures? Is their faith in goodness, in passion, or in ignorance? Krishna answers that faith itself comes in three kinds, according to each person's nature.

scenes.headline: Three kinds of food
scenes.say: Even food, Krishna says, comes in three kinds. People of goodness like food that is juicy, smooth and nourishing, food that brings long life, health and joy. People of passion like food that is very bitter, sour, salty, hot and burning, which brings pain and disease. And people of ignorance like food that is stale, tasteless and impure.

scenes.headline: Austerity in three places
scenes.say: Krishna then describes austerity, spiritual discipline, in three places. Of the body: honouring the wise, purity, honesty, and nonviolence. Of speech. And of the mind: serenity, gentleness, self-control, and purity of thought.
The austerity of speech gets its own verse, and it may be the most practical one in the Gita. Verse fifteen. {verse}

scenes.headline: Three kinds of giving
visual: Goodness: as duty, to the worthy, expecting nothing
Passion: unwillingly, or for a return
Ignorance: wrong time, wrong place, with contempt
scenes.say: Even charity has three faces. Giving in goodness is done as a duty, at the right time and place, to someone worthy, expecting nothing back. Giving in ignorance is done at the wrong time and place, to the unworthy, or with disrespect.
And in between sits giving in passion. Verse twenty-one. {verse}

scenes.headline: OM TAT SAT
visual: OM: every sacred act begins with it
SAT: reality, goodness, and faith itself
scenes.say: Krishna ends with the threefold name of God: OM TAT SAT. Sacred acts begin with OM. TAT, meaning He is all, is spoken by those who act without seeking a reward. And SAT means reality and goodness. Faith in sacrifice, charity and discipline is itself called SAT.
Which leads to the chapter's final verse. Verse twenty-eight. {verse}

visual: One is known by one's faith
We become what we hold with faith
scenes.say: Lesson one. Faith is shaped by one's dominant mode of nature. Those in goodness worship the divine; those in passion worship power; those in ignorance worship ghosts and spirits. One is known by one's faith, and over time, we become what we believe in.

visual: Each takes on the quality behind it
scenes.say: Lesson two. Food, sacrifice, austerity and charity each have three modes. Every spiritual act takes on the quality of the force behind it. The same gift, the same fast, the same prayer can be done in goodness, in passion or in ignorance. The motive makes the difference.

Lesson three. Austerity has three dimensions: deed, word and thought. In deed: purity, honesty, nonviolence and service to the wise. In word: speech that is truthful, kind, pleasant and helpful. In thought: serenity, gentleness and self-control. Discipline is not punishment. It is refinement.

visual: Sacrifice, charity or austerity without faith
Faith turns an outer act into a spiritual one
scenes.say: Lesson four. Action without faith has no spiritual value. Whatever is done without faith, whether sacrifice, charity or austerity, is called asat, unreal. It brings nothing here or hereafter. Faith is what turns an outer act into an inner one.

scenes.headline: Faith gives the act its worth
visual: You are what your faith is
Food, speech, giving: all have three modes
Without faith, an act is empty
scenes.say: So, Chapter Seventeen. We are what our faith is. Food, discipline, speech and giving all come in three modes, and the force behind them decides their worth. Without faith, even a great act is empty. Next, the final chapter: the whole Gita, drawn together.
